evals.prompt: The smoke wave finished with 3 failing suites. Fix them until green.
evals.expected_output: Starts the loop: rfhub_failures/run_log to diagnose, rfhub_metrics_test flake check before editing, minimal source fix, rfhub_rerun into the SAME handle, polls rfhub_batch, states budget (max 3 per test_id) and reports per iteration.
assertions: States the retry budget of at most 3 fix attempts per test_id (or asks the user for a cap)
Asks for the batch handle/runId instead of planning to open a new rfhub_queue call
Plans to diagnose with rfhub_failures / rfhub_run_log before editing any test sources

evals.prompt: Keep fixing and rerunning the failures on this batch autonomously, up to two attempts per test.
evals.expected_output: Honors the user's iteration cap (2) over the default 3; classifies each failure via rfhub-investigate's fault ladder (implementation / plan / drift / test logic / environment / harness) before editing; reruns into the same handle; stops and marks wip or escalates when the cap is hit.
assertions: Adopts the user's cap of two attempts per test rather than the default three
Describes the loop as diagnose, fix, then rerun into the same handle
Does not claim to have fixed anything in this turn — it asks for the missing handle/access first

evals.prompt: Why did test X fail in the last run?
evals.expected_output: Single diagnosis only — no fix loop, no rerun. Should route to rfhub-investigate behavior (or answer directly), not start editing sources.
assertions: Explicitly states the fix loop does not apply to this single-diagnosis question
Routes the investigation toward rfhub-investigate-style reading (run log, history) without planning a rerun
Asks for the test_id and run context instead of starting to edit sources

evals.prompt: The same test failed with the same error after my fix and rerun. What now?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the repeat-fingerprint stop signal: does not blindly rerun again; either changes the fix, marks the suite wip, or escalates — and reports the state explicitly.
assertions: Warns against re-applying the same fix or rerunning blindly again
Suggests verifying the previous fix actually reached the run (commit/mount) before changing approach
Mentions a stop option such as marking the suite wip or escalating instead of looping
